audit.scope: Repository architecture, backend dispatch, packaging, benchmark validity, documentation, CI surface, and migration readiness at PR23 head.

checklist.evidence: The PR23 tree has no files under .github/workflows; native reproducibility is carried by a separate artifact branch.
README describes JAX+diffrax and 129 tests while the current tree has a large PyO3/Rust runtime and a much larger test surface; _rustcore README still describes a hybrid silent-fallback boundary.
Backend selection is import-availability driven and broad import exceptions collapse to Python without a production hard-fail policy.
Cargo.lock and requirements.lock exist, but the root Python project and _rustcore use separate build entry points and the root pyproject leaves several scientific dependencies unpinned.
Existing focused and native receipts are strong; direct native consumers require the compatible wheel/vendor artifact, and performance evidence is host-contamination sensitive.
The extension has its own maturin project while the root project has no unified build backend guaranteeing a compatible native module.
Legacy plan and status documents overlap current architecture; PR23 correctly narrowed reruns but historical docs retain old backend and test-count claims.

findings.finding: The existing taskset/process-snapshot procedure does not make performance independent of external CPU use.
findings.evidence: Candidate B remained unmeasured because unrelated host work persisted; task affinity alone does not prove exclusive cores or isolate shared cache, memory, power, thermal, IRQ, or VM-steal effects.
findings.impact: Absolute speedup and scaling claims can be biased or blocked; clean paired causal claims require a stronger runner contract.

findings.finding: Supported production calls can silently select Python after any native import exception.
findings.evidence: bianchi/backend.py catches broad Exception at import and uses HAVE_RUST plus force_python flags; _rustcore README advertises quiet fallback.
findings.impact: ABI, packaging, or extension failures can become unexplained slowness and can hide which implementation produced a result.

findings.finding: Production numerical ownership is fragmented across Rust, NumPy/SciPy, JAX/diffrax, and repeated PyO3 entry points.
findings.evidence: Numerical modules remain under bianchi/charts, matter, q, rays, thermo, observables, analysis, integrate.py, and batch.py while parallel implementations exist under _rustcore/src.
findings.impact: FFI crossings, duplicated caches, incompatible threading, and backend drift limit optimization and make full-run provenance hard to state.

findings.finding: The PyO3 export/adapter surface is concentrated in a roughly 99 KB lib.rs despite domain modules existing below it.
findings.evidence: At PR23, _rustcore/src/lib.rs is 98,693 bytes and contains bindings for geometry, ODE, thermo, kinetic, tilted, Q, rays, and ensemble paths.
findings.impact: Ownership, review, compile isolation, and FFI safety become harder as the full runtime moves to Rust.

findings.finding: No checked-in GitHub workflow proves Python, native wheel, locked Cargo, portable CPU, or benchmark-harness contracts.
findings.evidence: The .github/workflows directory is empty at PR23 head.
findings.impact: The migration cannot rely on repeatable PR-level proof and platform regressions may be discovered only in manual audits.

findings.finding: Public setup and architecture documentation materially lags the current Rust runtime.
findings.evidence: Root README still describes JAX+diffrax and 129 tests; _rustcore README labels the project R0/R1 while its source exports much broader functionality.
findings.impact: Developers may install the wrong path, infer the wrong default backend, or repeat already completed work.

findings.finding: The Python and native package entry points do not guarantee one compatible installation unit.
findings.evidence: Root pyproject.toml declares Python dependencies while _rustcore/pyproject.toml separately owns maturin and module-name bianchi_rustcore.
findings.impact: A nominal Python install can omit or mismatch the required default backend.

findings.finding: GPU acceleration is an optional hypothesis, not established performance authority.
findings.evidence: Cargo declares an empty cuda feature and PR23 contains no accepted GPU implementation or transfer-inclusive measurement.
findings.impact: GPU work must not displace the portable CPU closure or be selected by default.

findings.finding: The R5b acceptance observable has already been corrected without weakening scientific authority.
findings.evidence: PR21 records 34 focused PASS under operator, direct-state, residual, independent-science, and no-fallback checks.
findings.impact: Do not reopen the retired error-of-error comparator or rerun R5b absent a changed closure.

findings.finding: The pre-migration source, symbolic candidate, and native reproduction payload are remotely pinned.
findings.evidence: Two archive refs were created at exact PR23 and PR22 heads and native r2 remains pinned by branch, commit, archive, wheel, and Cargo.lock digests.
findings.impact: Every migration phase has an explicit recovery source without duplicating raw evidence in human reports.

findings.finding: The PR23 performance corpus is not representative of the requested whole-runtime migration.
findings.evidence: The recorded corpus is dominated by the already coarse-call Q and R5b paths; it does not expose Python-owned geometry preparation, background, rays, thermo, observables, startup, allocation, or batch overhead as separate or end-to-end strata.
findings.impact: Optimizing against the legacy corpus can report a local win while leaving most supported production execution in Python or making unmeasured paths slower.

findings.finding: Importing the top-level Python package eagerly initializes JAX policy even when Rust is the requested backend.
findings.evidence: bianchi/__init__.py imports JAX and enables x64 at import time at the audited head.
findings.impact: The Rust-default frontend pays optional accelerator startup and dependency cost, and backend selection is no longer an isolated capability decision.

target_architecture.name: RUST_REQUIRED_NUMERICAL_RUNTIME_WITH_PYTHON_FRONTEND
principles: One production source of numerical execution truth: Rust.
Python oracle is independent, explicit, slow, and never a silent fallback.
Symbolic/Wolfram/SymPy compilers remain offline formula authorities, not runtime dependencies.
Cross the FFI once per user-intent operation, never once per integrator step or angular node.
Use dependency-connected subsystem closures rather than isolated micro-hotspot patches.
Correctness, architecture closure, and performance materiality are separate decisions.
Portable scalar behavior remains available under every optimization.
No optimization may redefine a scientific invariant or acceptance observable.

rust_runtime.state_ownership: Validated immutable configuration and mutable numerical state are created once in Rust and remain Rust-owned until coarse result extraction.
rust_runtime.workspace_policy: Preallocate and reuse scratch buffers, solver state, quadrature tables, coefficient tables, thread pools, and dispatch decisions. No allocation in declared inner loops.
rust_runtime.error_policy: Typed Rust errors cross PyO3 with domain context; panics never cross FFI; unsupported configurations fail closed.

ffi.technology: PyO3 0.29 plus rust-numpy 0.29 at the locked baseline
rules: Borrow contiguous NumPy input read-only without a copy when layout and dtype match.
Validate shape, dtype, alignment, finiteness, and aliasing once at entry.
Copy or reject explicitly when zero-copy preconditions fail; report which occurred.
Detach from Python for Rust-only work before Rayon or long integrator execution.
Return owned contiguous arrays or fill a validated writable output buffer.
Do not hold Python references, the GIL, or Python locks inside Rayon work.
Split lib.rs into domain binding modules with no numerical implementation in adapters.

data_layout.default: Contiguous f64 structure-of-arrays for wide independent lanes; compact array-of-structs only for small fixed state vectors when measurements and vectorization reports support it.
rules: No Vec<Vec<T>> in production inner paths.
Use fixed-size arrays or nalgebra stack types for small known tensors.
Use flat aligned buffers with explicit shape metadata for grids and hierarchies.
Represent rank-l PSTF coefficients in the canonical 2*l+1 independent-component layout; do not expand to 3^l Cartesian storage in production inner loops.
Cache immutable basis, coefficient, quadrature, and generated-kernel data by exact manifest identity.
Make units, conventions, and state ordering typed or validated at the boundary.
Record peak resident memory and allocation counts for every migrated subsystem.

parallelism.default_strategy: Coarse deterministic parallelism across independent ensemble members, rays, modes, species, or grid tiles before inner-kernel parallelism.
parallelism.thread_pool: One explicitly constructed and owned Rayon ThreadPool per runtime context; do not rely on an ambient global pool for authority or benchmarks.
rules: Pin or size the pool once before measurement.
Force OpenMP, BLAS, MKL, BLIS, NumExpr, and other nested pools to one thread unless they are the sole declared parallel owner.
Avoid nested Rayon parallel iterators; outer owner passes a serial inner policy.
Partition by stable indices and collect in stable order.
Use deterministic pairwise or compensated reductions where reductions affect accepted outputs.
Keep a serial Rust path for differential and portability checks.
Parallel work must be coarse enough to amortize pool and scheduling overhead.

simd.portable_authority: Stable scalar loops structured for LLVM autovectorization.
runtime_variants: x86_64_avx512 only as a separately measured optional variant
aarch64_neon when a supported runner exists
simd.dispatch: Runtime feature detection with std::arch and per-function target_feature; cache the selected function pointer in the RuntimePlan.
proof: Inspect emitted vectorization reports or assembly for claimed SIMD kernels.
Run scalar-versus-dispatched differential tests under the state/operator/residual/invariant contract.
Measure wall time plus instructions/cycles; fewer instructions without a clean wall-time result is mechanistic support only.
Retain scalar fallback on every supported target.

scientific_acceptance.floating_point_rule: SIMD and parallel reductions may change low bits; validate primitive state, operators, residuals, invariants, and independent accuracy with predeclared scale-aware budgets.
scientific_acceptance.tolerance_rule: Reuse existing scientific tolerances. Any proposed tolerance or reference change is a separate PI decision and cannot be bundled with optimization.
scientific_acceptance.no_fallback_rule: Every supported rust_required test asserts that the Python oracle was not called.

performance_protocol.truth_boundary: Literal independence from external CPU use is unavailable on a shared host. Exclusive cpusets reduce scheduler co-tenancy but do not isolate shared LLC, memory controller, power, thermal, firmware, IRQ, or hypervisor effects.

risk_register.mitigation: One SPEC/EVIDENCE machine authority, short README, short HANDOFF, pointer-only PR body.
risk_register.stop: Human docs exceed budgets or repeat raw hash inventories.

anti_accretion.machine_authority: SPEC.json for this plan and one EVIDENCE.json per implementation node.
anti_accretion.rule: Machine-readable evidence must be referenced, not reproduced, in human closeout.
forbidden: per-part archive hashes in human reports
full command transcripts in PR body

delivery.rollback: Revert the node commit or reset a fresh worktree to the previous stacked head; archive refs remain untouched.
